GROUND RULES: ATTENTION ALL CONTESTANTS - Contestants must have their 2027 membership renewed to be accepted as entries for the Dever Qualifier.
ALL EVENTS - The "30-hour replacement" policy will be in effect. See Rodeo Entry Information page of the business journal.
ALL CONTESTANTS - All participants agree to be bound by the terms and conditions of the PRCA Bylaws and Official Rodeo Rules and these Ground Rules.
ALL CONTESTANTS - All contestants must check-in with the rodeo secretary in the "Show Office" and sign a release of liability before competing in this rodeo.

ALL CONTESTANTS WITH HORSES - Must have proof of current Coggins test and current health papers. Health papers must be checked at the Stalling Office prior to unloading horses. All stalls will be available to contestants at $20 per night (includes one bag of shavings), beginning Monday, October 19 after 4:00 p.m., on a first come first served basis. Parking of contestant's vehicles and horse trailers must be in area designated by the National Western Stock Show parking lot operator.
TD, SW, and TR Qualifications for Denver, CO - January 14-24, 2027 and the Denver Qualifier - October 20-22, 2026:
80 minimum entries for the Denver Rodeo. No compensation. No slack. No exemptions.

The top 30 in the final 2026 PRCA World Standings, the top 5 who enter based on 2027 money won, the top 5 from the 2026 Mountain States Circuit Standings who enter and who are not already qualified in the previous two categories, and 40 from the Denver Qualifier (October 20-22) will be accepted as entries for a total of 80 entries for the Denver Rodeo. The contestants who were among the top 30 in the final 2026 World Standings in each event will be accepted as entries for the Denver rodeo if they enter and will not be accepted as entries for the Qualifier. All others may enter the Denver Qualifier on October 20-22. If not all of the top 30 from the 2026 PRCA World Standings in an event enter the Denver Rodeo, the remaining unfilled positions will be filled by contestants based on 2027 money won (not to exceed a total of 80 entries). For example, if only 28 from the Final 2026 World Standings enter the Denver Rodeo, 7 will be accepted based on 2027 money won, 5 from the 2026 Mountain States Circuit Standings, and 40 from the Denver Qualifier, for a total of 80. In the Team Roping, headers and heelers will qualify separately using the same qualifications The 80 headers who qualify must rope with the 80 heelers who qaulify. There will be a grace period for Team Ropers to designate partners. If a contestant qualifies as one of the top 5 from the 2026 Mountain States Circuit Standings after the completion of the Mountain States Circuit Finals on October 23 and 24 or qualifies for the 2027 money won qualification category, and is also one of the top 40 who advances through the Qualifier, he will be accepted as a Circuit qualifier or as a 2027 money won qualifier, and the next contestant from the Denver Qualifier based on fastest times in the average will be accepted to fill that position.
QUALIFICATIONS for the Denver Qualifier: TD - 145 minimum entries; SW - 155 minimum entries; TR - 120 minimum entries.

FORMAT: 40 qualifying contestants or teams from the qualifier will be placed in the performances at the National Western Stock Show, along with the 40 contestants (or teams) already entered. The 40 qualifying contestants or teams will be top ten from the first go-round (plus splits), the top ten from the second go-round that have not already qualified from the first go-round (plus splits), and the remaining positions (not to exceed 40) will be filled from the fastest times in the average after the first and second go-rounds. If there are ties, the tied contestant (or team) with the single fastest time will advance to the performances at the National Western Rodeo. If still tied, the tied contestant with the highest ranking in the 2026 PRCA World Standings for that event will advance. All 80 contestants (or teams) that qualify for the Denver National Western Rodeo will have a grace period to change preferences and/or buddy groups on Wed., Dec. 16 between 9 AM and 4 PM.
TD - Two go-rounds. Both run Tues., Oct. 20 at 9 AM.
TD - There will be a disqualification for a jerk down as long as criteria are in compliance with the jerk down policy.
SW - Two go-rounds. Both run Wed., Oct. 21 at 9 AM.
TR - Only two loops allowed.
TR - Two go-rounds. Both run Thurs., Oct. 22 at 9 AM.

SW - The steer must fall clean when a throw is attempted. If a clean fall is not achieved and the motion stops, the steer must be allowed to regain his feet before being thrown. If the steer is not allowed to regain his feet when instructed by the judge, the contestant will be disqualified.
TD, SW - $30 stock charge for cards and permits.
TR - $15 stock charge per man for cards and permits.
TE - The qualifier and the National Western Rodeo performances will each count as separate rodeos. All entries are official, unless contestant specifies otherwise at time of entry.
TD, SW, TR - Payoff will be in accordance with the rule book.
STK CONT.: Various

PRCA/WRPA co-approved rodeos (held outside of the MLC) will count as money won but will not be included in rodeo count towards qualifying for the Maple Leaf Circuit Finals.

Contestants, stock contractors and contract personnel do not need a PRCA/WPRA membership to compete/work rodeos within the Maple Leaf Circuit unless they want to compete/work at the NFR or National Circuit Finals

If there are less than 3 qualified scores or times in one or more of the brackets, the contestant with the highest score or fastest time in his section of brackets who has not already qualified in the top 3 of his respective bracket will advance. This process will be repeated until all positions in the semi-finals are filled. The brackets will be divided into two sections. Section one includes brackets 1, 2, 3, and 4, and section two includes brackets 5, 6, 7, and 8. If there are less than 12 qualified rides in section one of the brackets or section two of the brackets, a random draw by the judges following the completion of each of the two sections will determine which contestants with no score will be advanced to the semi-finals to insure that there are 24 contestants to fill the semi-finals. The semi-finals will include 24 contestants competing in the 17th, 18th, and 19th performances (8 per performance) all occurring on Saturday, January 23. A contestant must compete in all go-rounds in order to advance to the semi-finals or the finals (does not include VIR's and DR's).
